c: Redstone Plumbing Supply, a wholesale supplier serving 300 contractors
s: Redstone Plumbing Supply buys pipe, valves and fixtures from many vendors and sells them on credit to contractors. Invoices are sometimes paid twice and sometimes late, and customers' balances are not always up to date.

The controller (judge) wants you to explain how accurate records of accounts payable and accounts receivable keep the company healthy, and how you would organize the information so errors are found quickly.
p: Explain the nature of accounts payable
Explain the nature of accounts receivable
Account for purchases
Maintain financial records
Organize information
n: Accounts payable are amounts owed to vendors; receivable are amounts owed by customers
Matches purchase orders, receiving reports and invoices before paying
Uses an aging report to follow up on late customers and to pay vendors on time
Keeps records in a consistent system with dates, amounts and approvals
q: You find a vendor invoice that was paid twice. What do you do?
Why is it important to separate the person who orders from the person who pays invoices?

c: Hollis Family Dental, a four-dentist practice
s: Hollis Family Dental's bank balance never matches its books at the end of the month. Staff are not sure whether the difference comes from timing, mistakes or something else, and the administrator is uneasy about how cash is handled.

The practice administrator (judge) wants you to explain how to read and reconcile bank statements, how to protect cash from errors or theft, and why the practice should produce regular financial statements.
p: Read and reconcile bank statements
Describe the nature of cash flow statements
Discuss the role of ethics in accounting
Explain the use of technology in accounting
Describe the need for financial information
n: Compares each deposit and check with the bank statement and lists outstanding items
Reconciliation adjusts for fees, interest, errors and timing
Controls: dual approval, daily deposits, limited access and surprise reviews
Accounting software automates entries, reports and backups
Statements help owners make decisions and secure loans
q: What would you do if you found a check you could not match to any expense?
How often should the practice reconcile its bank account, and why?

c: BrightPath Learning Center, a childcare and tutoring center with 35 employees
s: BrightPath Learning Center pays staff biweekly by hand-calculated checks. Last month two employees were paid incorrectly and the owner is not sure the center withheld the right taxes.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain how payroll works, what deductions and tax obligations the center has, and how to make payroll accurate, timely and legal.
p: Interpret a pay stub
Explain the nature of tax liabilities
Explain legal considerations for accounting
Maintain financial records
Explain the use of technology in accounting
n: Gross pay minus withholdings equals net pay; stubs show each item
Employers withhold income tax and payroll taxes and pay their share on time
Records must be kept and filed on schedule; mistakes can bring penalties
Payroll software reduces errors and creates reports
Keeps confidential data secure
q: An employee says their paycheck is too low. What do you do?
What could happen if the center misclassifies a worker as a contractor?

s: Maplewood Boutique Hotel's CFO learned that a department manager has been asking vendors to backdate invoices so spending falls into the next quarter and the department stays under budget.
The CFO (judge) wants you to explain why accurate, honest accounting matters, what laws and ethical standards apply, and how you would respond if you were asked to record something misleading.
p: Discuss the role of ethics in accounting
Explain legal considerations for accounting
Demonstrate honesty and integrity
Recognize and respond to ethical dilemmas
Describe the need for financial information
n: Users of financial information, including lenders and owners, rely on it being accurate
Accounting rules, laws and audits exist to prevent misleading information
Refuses to record false entries and reports the request through the proper channel
Considers the consequences for the company, the manager and the associate
q: The manager says everyone does it and nobody gets hurt. What do you say?
What would you do if the CFO's boss asked you to do the same thing?

c: Cascade Outdoor Education, a nonprofit that runs wilderness camps
s: Cascade Outdoor Education had a $60,000 deficit last year. Camp fees have not changed in four years while costs for insurance, food and gear have risen, and donations fluctuate.
The executive director (judge) wants you to explain how a budget helps manage the organization, how you would analyze results against the budget, and what actions you would recommend.
p: Describe the nature of budgets
Describe the nature of income statements
Determine factors affecting business risk
Explain the role of finance in business
Interpret statistical findings
n: A budget is a plan for income and expenses used to guide decisions
Compares actual to budget, finds variances and explains them
Considers fixed and variable costs, seasonality and donor reliance
Recommends changes such as fee increases, cost control and new funding
q: Would you raise fees or cut costs first? Why?
How would you explain a deficit to donors honestly?
